final_message:
I fixed one bug in `wrap` in `src/wrap.py`. I haven't run it or any tests.

When a word was longer than `width` and the current line was empty, `wrap` added an empty string to the output before the word. For example, `wrap("supercalifragilistic hi", 5)` started with a blank line. The check now only closes the current line if it has content, so an over-long word goes on its own line without a blank one before it.

I left over-long words unbroken rather than splitting them mid-word. If your users expect hard splitting at `width`, that would be a separate change. Tell me if you want it.

I only found this one bug. If users are seeing other wrong results, send me an example input and the output they expected.
